articles.title: Holo Prism Shift
articles.summary: Fine prism flecks with angular facet clusters that sweep rainbow as the view angle changes. Reads as a clean metallic or satin sheen with a faint prismatic-looking twinkle only where the sun hits; nothing visible as a pattern.
articles.what: Holographic prism flecks 4-10 px with per-fleck rainbow CC sweep + 6-12 angular facet cluster zones 16-22 px for view-angle shift, M=Metallic + G=Roughness + B=Clearcoat Up close: Almost smooth in this grey lit render: a very sparse, tiny scatter of pinpoint glints and a few short slivers inside the highlight, with faint facet clusters you can barely see. The rainbow sweep the description talks about is a view-angle effect that a grey render cannot show. From a distance: Reads as a clean metallic or satin sheen with a faint prismatic-looking twinkle only where the sun hits; nothing visible as a pattern. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Holographic & Color-Shift (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Holographic & Color-Shift", or search for "Holo Prism Shift".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: flecks catch light on open panels
Best over dark metallic bases where glints stand out
Numbers keep their colour; flecks are sparse so legibility is unaffected.
Almost no visible change; a few glints in the highlight
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a rainbow paint: it adds no colour itself, the shift comes from reflected light angles
Not holographic flake: flecks are much sparser and finer than a flake pack
Avoid: reads as noise at distance, fights busy liveries.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Holo Prism Shift over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
